title: Decision of the AI Office
summary: The AI Office’s decision outlines its criteria for approving AI initiatives, detailing how it assesses feasibility, safety, and impact. It also establishes responsibilities and monitoring protocols to ensure responsible use and compliance with ethical standards.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Technology Specialists in AI
summary: The document announces a vacancy for Technology Specialists in AI within the AI Office, outlining the roles and responsibilities expected of candidates. It also provides guidance on the qualifications, skills, and ethical considerations required for new hires to support the organization’s AI initiatives.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Lead Scientific Adviser
summary: This policy explains the opening for a Lead Scientific Adviser in the AI Office and the purpose of the role. It outlines the qualifications, responsibilities, and expectations for the person who will fill the position.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Legal Officers
summary: The policy explains what is expected from legal officers at the AI office, including their duties, qualifications, and how they should handle legal matters. It also covers rules for using AI responsibly, ensuring compliance with laws, and managing risk.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Policy Officers
summary: The document announces open positions for AI Policy Officers, outlining the duties, qualifications, and expected contributions of these roles. It also details the application procedure, selection criteria, and how the new officers will support the organization’s AI strategy and compliance efforts.

title: AI Act Scientific Panel
summary: The AI Act Scientific Panel is a group of experts tasked with advising on the legal and technical aspects of AI regulation. They review AI technologies, assess risks, and recommend safeguards to ensure AI systems are safe, transparent, and aligned with European values.

title: Draft Standardisation Request
summary: This draft policy outlines a formal request process for standardising AI systems across industries, detailing the criteria and procedures that organisations must follow to achieve consistency. It also identifies key stakeholders, compliance checkpoints, and accountability measures to ensure transparent and safe AI deployment.

title: CoP Consultation Notice
summary: The CoP Consultation Notice invites stakeholders to share feedback on proposed policies. It outlines the consultation process, timelines, and how to submit comments.

title: CoP Call for Expression of Interest
summary: The document invites individuals and organizations to express interest in forming or joining a Community of Practice (CoP) focused on AI policy. It outlines the purpose, expected outcomes, and steps for interested parties to get involved.

title: CoP Graphic: Overview of Iterative Drafting Process
summary: The policy document presents a graphic that outlines the iterative drafting process used by the Community of Practice (CoP). It shows the key stages—initial drafting, peer review, revision, and final approval—emphasizing collaboration and continuous improvement at each step.

title: CoP Graphic: Timeline of Drafting Process
summary: This document presents a graphic timeline that illustrates the key stages of the drafting process for the policy. It visually traces the sequence of decisions, revisions, and approvals that occurred from start to finish.

title: Code of Practice: 1st Draft
summary: The Code of Practice: 1st Draft sets out initial rules and standards for the ethical development and use of AI. It covers key areas such as transparency, fairness, accountability, and data protection to guide stakeholders in responsible AI practices.

title: Code of Practice: 2nd Draft
summary: This document presents the second draft of a Code of Practice, setting out guidelines for responsible and ethical use of AI. It refines earlier standards to enhance transparency, accountability, and best practices for all stakeholders.

title: Code of Practice: 3rd Draft
summary: This is the third draft of a Code of Practice that sets out guidelines for how to develop, deploy, and use artificial intelligence responsibly. It provides best‑practice steps, ethical principles, and compliance checks that organizations should follow to ensure safe, trustworthy AI systems.

title: AI Pact Draft
summary: The AI Pact Draft proposes a set of agreements among stakeholders to promote responsible, safe, and transparent AI development. It seeks to establish collaborative standards and guidelines to ensure ethical use of AI technologies.

title: AI Pact Final
summary: The AI Pact Final is a set of agreements that set out how AI should be built, used, and regulated, stressing safety, fairness, and transparency. It defines roles for governments, companies, and the public, and establishes rules and oversight to make sure those commitments are followed.

title: Guidelines on prohibited artificial intelligence (AI) practices
summary: This guideline document specifies the AI practices that are prohibited, such as deceptive automation, discrimination, and privacy violations. It serves as a reference for companies to ensure their AI systems comply with ethical standards and regulatory requirements.

title: Guidelines on AI System Definition
summary: This document provides guidelines for defining AI systems, outlining key characteristics and components that distinguish AI from non‑AI solutions. It helps organizations align their AI system definitions with regulatory and industry standards.

title: Communication on Boosting Start-Ups & Innovation
summary: The policy focuses on improving communication strategies to support the growth of start‑ups and drive innovation across the sector. It outlines initiatives such as networking events, shared resources, and public‑private partnerships aimed at creating a collaborative ecosystem that nurtures new businesses.

title: EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups
summary: The EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups aims to provide high‑performance computing resources and support to emerging AI and tech companies across Europe. It offers access to cutting‑edge infrastructure, mentorship, and funding opportunities to accelerate their growth and innovation.

title: Slideshow: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: This webinar uses a slideshow to teach participants about risk management fundamentals. Attendees will learn how to identify, assess, and mitigate risks in various settings.

title: Video: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: The webinar video covers strategies for spotting and reducing risks in AI projects, such as using governance guidelines and compliance checks. It also shows practical ways to evaluate potential threats and put in place controls to keep AI systems safe.
